java_locations: abel/Link.java#getEntityPort (227-231): every endpoint whose EntityPosition.usePortP() holds (abel/EntityPosition.java 186-188: ENTRY_POINT, EXIT_POINT, ports) is written as EntityPort.forPort(uid), i.e. 'uid:P' (cucadiagram/EntityPort.java 54-63); svek/SvekEdge.java (391-393) prints getFullString() for both ends. This holds for short and wide labels alike.

svek/SvekNode.java#appendLabelHtmlSpecialForPort (180-187): label width (int) > 40 gives the plaintext HTML table whose centre cell carries PORT="P" (appendLabelHtmlSpecialForPortHtml 189-205); otherwise appendLabelHtmlSpecialForPortBasic (207-220) declares a plain shape=rect with no port, so dot reports 'node <uid>, port P unrecognized' for Java's own DOT.

dot/AbstractGraphviz.java#createFile3 (97-134): dot runs through ProcessRunner, whose error stream is captured and never written; the isCheckDotError reporting is commented out (123-133). Java's CLI stderr therefore never carries dot diagnostics.

svek/DotStringFactory.java#solve (363-369): a RECTANGLE_PORT node's corner is the minimum of the first points list after its <title>; svek/SvekNode.java#getRectangleArea/getPointCenter use that corner and the image dimension (EntityImageStateBorder, 2*EntityPosition.RADIUS square).

svek/Cluster.java#manageEntryExitPoint (411-433): the frontier passes through sh.getRectangleArea().getPointCenter() of each border node; svek/SvekResult.java#drawU (82-89) draws the EntityImageStateBorder at (minX, minY), so the circle centre is that same point; svek/image/EntityImageStateBorder.java#drawU (79-106) places the label from that corner (x = -(descWidth - 2*RADIUS)/2, above or below by upPosition).
The same GraphvizImageBuilder/DotStringFactory serves the root and every GroupMakerState image (svek/GroupMakerState.java 140-152), so image border points follow the root rule.
rust_locations: crates/rustuml-render/src/state.rs#apply_state_border_frontiers and #render_non_autarkic_root_clusters: the root path already takes the border point's centre as the solved layout node centre plus state_position_image_offset_x (the shielded table's P-cell offset, svek_state_border_geometry), matching Java.

crates/rustuml-render/src/state.rs#layout_autonomous_scope (positions loop) and #autonomous_scope_painted_bounds: the image path takes the corner of the solved layout node plus half of node_sizes (12x12). For a shielded port the solved node is the table (layout_width x 36), so the circle lands at (6 - layout_width/2, 6 - 18) from the frontier: (-21, -12) for the 54-wide minimum table of img_cluster_exit_wide. Short labels have a 12x12 layout node and are unaffected.
vendor/graphviz/lib/cgraph/agerror.c#default_usererrf: the in-process Graphviz writes every agerr/agwarningf diagnostic to the CLI's stderr, where Java's ProcessRunner swallows dot's.
invariant: Inside an image, a border point's circle centre is the solved node centre plus the P-cell offset (identical to the root path and to the frontier input), its painted bounds and label start from centre - RADIUS, and the CLI's stderr carries no Graphviz diagnostics, as Java's does not. The DOT keeps Java's 'uid:P' for every entry/exit point.

autonomous_scope_painted_bounds: the circle corner and label anchor of a port node derive from the same centre (centre - RADIUS).
rustuml-layout: install a discarding agusererrf through agseterrf once per process before Graphviz is used, mirroring createFile3's captured-and-dropped error stream. No DOT text changes.
